name: ozen-hebrew-lexicon
description: Israeli spoken Hebrew lexicon for speech-to-text translation: slang and discourse markers, Hebrew-transliterated programming vocabulary, and the morphology traps that defeat naive dictionary lookup.

provenance.live_corpus: ~/Library/Application Support/ai.orellius.ozen/log.json - 70 utterances, 69 translate + 1 repair, all lang=he, mean whisper confidence 0.886, 0 operator corrections. Read 2026-08-06.
external: he.wiktionary.org - individual entries fetched 2026-08-06 where marked; 25,175 content pages, 53 active editors in 30 days (https://he.wiktionary.org/wiki/Special:Statistics, verified 2026-08-06)
Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif, Keter 2005, ~10,000 entries (https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI, verified 2026-08-06). Not machine-readable, not licensed for reuse.

Academy of the Hebrew Language terms bank - ~120,000 terms in ~240 dictionaries, Hebrew paired with English (https://terms.hebrew-academy.org.il/Home/About, verified 2026-08-06 via browser; the site returns 403 to crawlers). NO public API or bulk download is documented.

honesty.source_verified: Entries whose `source` names a fetched URL with a verification date were read on that date.
honesty.not_verified: Entries whose `source` says 'author knowledge, NOT source-verified' are translations the author is confident in but did not confirm against a citable source. They are marked rather than dropped because a working lexicon that admits its weak entries is more useful than a short one that hides them - but they must not be treated as evidence.
known_gaps: The he.wiktionary pages for וואלה, לפרגן and פרגון return HTTP 404; those three entries are not individually verified.

No Hebrew-English code-switching corpus exists in LinCE, CALCS, or the Israeli national Hebrew-resources index (https://github.com/NNLP-IL/Hebrew-Resources, verified 2026-08-06). There is no dataset to validate the code-switching entries against.

The dev-transliteration Hebrew spellings are the ones ASR actually produces, which is not the same as the spellings a Hebrew speaker would write. Variants are listed where observed; the list is certainly incomplete.

entries.interpreter: come on  |  let's go  |  alright (closing a topic)
entries.notes: Four distinct senses in one token: (1) urging - 'come on'; (2) agreement - 'alright'; (3) skeptical dismissal - 'yeah, right'; (4) leave-taking / topic-closing - 'okay, we're done here'. In dictation it is overwhelmingly sense 4 at the START of an utterance ('yalla, do X') where the correct English is to DROP it entirely or render 'okay,'. Arabic yalla < ya Allah.
entries.source: he.wiktionary יאללה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: cool  |  sounds good  |  fine by me
entries.notes: Adverb and adjective, invariable. Both an evaluation ('it's good') and an acknowledgement token ('okay, got it'). As a standalone reply it is pure acknowledgement and carries no content: in a dictation destined for a terminal it should usually be dropped. Arabic sababa; the French 'ca va bien' story is folk etymology per the entry.
entries.source: he.wiktionary סבבה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Adjective, INVARIABLE and PRE-nominal, which is unusual for Hebrew - 'אחלה בילד' = 'great build', not 'build great'. A parser that assumes Hebrew adjectives follow their noun mis-attaches it. Arabic ahla (comparative of hilw, sweet).
entries.source: he.wiktionary אחלה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Discourse particle of surprise, mild confirmation, or reluctant agreement. Sense is carried almost entirely by intonation, which the ASR discards - so a text-only pipeline CANNOT disambiguate it. Safest policy for dictation: drop it. Arabic wallah, 'by God'. Spelled וואלה / ואללה / וללה; the וואלה page 404s on he.wiktionary, so this entry is not individually verified.
entries.source: he.wiktionary ואללה (not individually fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Adverb. Marks the shift from discussion to the operative point, which is exactly the sentence a dictation user wants kept. Rendering it as 'purpose' or leaving it transliterated is the classic failure. Yiddish pronunciation of Hebrew תכלית; the unstressed final ת became ס. Spelled תכלס / תכל'ס.
entries.source: he.wiktionary תכלס (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Interjection of exasperation or emphasis. Contraction of בוא הנה ('come here'). Carries no propositional content; drop it in dictation.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.interpreter: it's terrible  |  it's in bad shape
entries.notes: Idiom, predicative. 'הבילד על הפנים' = 'the build is broken/terrible', NOT 'the build is on the face'. This is the single most literal-translatable-into-nonsense idiom in the everyday set.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: amazing (positive)  |  forget it, not worth it (older negative sense)
entries.notes: POLARITY-AMBIGUOUS and the hardest single item in this lexicon. he.wiktionary lists a slang POSITIVE sense ('especially good') and an archaic NEGATIVE sense ('bad, a waste of time'). Modern Israeli speech is overwhelmingly positive-intensifier. Disambiguation needs the surrounding clause; the literal 'a pity about the time' is always wrong.
entries.source: he.wiktionary חבל על הזמן (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Literal sense is a real bomb; slang senses are 'excellent' and 'physically attractive'. In a dev dictation, 'הבילד יצא פצצה' = 'the build came out great'. The literal reading is not merely wrong, it is alarming in a security or ops context - a real reason to get this one right.
entries.source: he.wiktionary פצצה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Negation idiom, also used as an exclamation of disbelief. 'אין מצב שזה עובד' = 'there's no way this works'.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Yiddish-derived prompting particle. Almost never carries content in dictation; drop it. Repeated 'נו נו נו' is impatience, not emphasis.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.interpreter: no big deal  |  keep it light  |  just a small one
entries.notes: Adverbial. 'תעשה את זה בקטנה' = 'do a quick/small version of it' - a scoping instruction, so dropping it loses real information in a dev context.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Feminine noun, Arabic fadiha ('scandal'). Distinct from פשלה: פדיחה is SOCIAL embarrassment, פשלה is an operational failure. Collapsing them into 'mistake' loses the register.
entries.source: he.wiktionary פדיחה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: a screw-up  |  a blunder with consequences
entries.notes: Feminine noun, Arabic fashal ('failure'). An operational failure with consequences - stronger than 'bug', weaker than 'outage'. 'עשיתי פשלה' = 'I messed up'.
entries.source: he.wiktionary פשלה (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Arabic khafif ('light'). 'עשית את זה חפיף' = 'you did it sloppily'. A quality judgement, and in dev dictation usually a complaint about the work just delivered.
entries.source: he.wiktionary חפיף (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: actually  |  of all things  |  deliberately (context decides)
entries.notes: The hardest word in everyday Hebrew for MT. he.wiktionary gives three senses: classical 'precisely', modern 'especially / contrary to expectation' ('why me of all people?'), and modern 'deliberately'. It is a scope-and-contrast operator, not a content word; a fixed gloss is wrong in at least a third of occurrences. Aramaic דַּוְקָא.
entries.source: he.wiktionary דווקא (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: that's perfectly fine  |  no problem at all
entries.notes: Intensified בסדר. Note the trap: בסדר alone is 'okay/fine', but as a question 'בסדר?' it is 'is that okay?', and as a response it is agreement. Register is neutral, not slang.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.notes: he.wiktionary explicitly labels the modern sense a discourse marker used 'to reduce tension and formality'. It is the Hebrew equivalent of English filler 'like'. In dictation it should be DELETED, not translated - translating it as 'as if' inverts the meaning of the clause. Classical sense ('as though') survives in written registers, so blanket deletion is wrong in formal text.
entries.source: he.wiktionary כאילו (fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Arabic ya'ni. Two jobs: a filler like כאילו, and a DISMISSIVE marker ('the so-called fix'). The dismissive reading changes the sentence's stance, so it cannot be blanket-dropped the way כאילו can.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.notes: As an INTENSIFIER before an adjective ('מה זה יפה' = 'it's incredibly nice') it is not the question 'what is this'. Position disambiguates: intensifier reading only when immediately followed by an adjective or adverb.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Resignation marker. In dictation it usually means 'drop this thread, move on' - an actionable instruction that a literal rendering destroys.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.interpreter: I'm fed up  |  I've had it with this
entries.notes: Dative-experiencer construction: the subject is the situation, the speaker is the dative. Word-for-word output is ungrammatical English. Same frame family as 'בא לי' (I feel like), 'אכפת לי' (I care), 'נמאס לי' (I'm sick of it) - all need re-subjectification.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.interpreter: he gives credit generously  |  he is happy for you
entries.notes: Yiddish-derived farginen, itself from German goennen ('to not begrudge'). NO single-word English equivalent - it is the absence of envy plus active praise. Rendering it 'complimentary' loses the 'without envy' component, which is the whole word. The לפרגן / מפרגן he.wiktionary pages 404, so this is not individually verified.
entries.source: he.wiktionary לפרגן (not individually fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Nominalisation of לפרגן. Same untranslatability. In Israeli work speech 'בלי פרגון' is a real criticism of a person, not a description of feedback volume.
entries.source: he.wiktionary פרגון (not individually fetched 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Marked עממי (colloquial), not slang, on he.wiktionary. Persian bala-khana -> Russian balagan -> Polish -> Yiddish -> Hebrew. Common in dev speech for a disorganised codebase or process: 'הקוד בלגן'.

entries.notes: Imperative + prepositional pronoun. Note the second person inflects: סמכי עליי (f.), סמכו עליי (pl.). ASR often produces the wrong gender form here because the vowels differ but the consonant skeleton barely does.

entries.notes: Adjective 'safe/certain' AND an adverbial 'definitely'. In security contexts the ambiguity is real and dangerous: 'זה בטוח' can be 'that's secure' or 'that's definitely so'. Needs the surrounding predicate.

entries.interpreter: just  |  never mind  |  for no reason
entries.notes: Three jobs: minimiser ('just a quick thing'), retraction ('never mind, I was kidding'), and pejorative ('it's pointless'). The retraction sense is dangerous in dictation - it CANCELS the preceding clause, so dropping it inverts the utterance.
entries.source: Rosenthal, Milon HaSlang HaMakif (Keter 2005), ISBN 9789650714017 - https://www.nli.org.il/en/books/NNL_ALEPH990024940280205171/NLI (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.notes: Neutral register, unlike אחלה/פצצה. Common acknowledgement of a completed task.

entries.notes: Closing marker. In dictation it usually means 'end of instruction' and is a good candidate for an utterance-final boundary cue rather than translated text.

entries.interpreter: a whole thing  |  weird  |  a bit (of behaviour)

entries.name: Conjunction clitic ו-
entries.notes: UD Hebrew splits the conjunction ו off as its own token. A glossary keyed on קומיט does not match the surface string וקומיט. Google's and DeepL's glossaries both match on surface strings and neither documents inflection handling, so an exact-match glossary misses every prefixed occurrence.

entries.name: Definite article ה-

entries.name: Covert definite after ב / ל / כ
en: in a house OR in the house
entries.notes: THE most-cited Hebrew ambiguity and it is documented in UD verbatim: 'the definite marker _ה, when appearing after the case markers ב or ל, is covert'. There is NO orthographic difference between 'in a repo' and 'in the repo'. English forces a choice the Hebrew never made, so any he->en engine is guessing on every such phrase. Neither a glossary nor a phrase table can fix this; only discourse context can.
entries.source: https://universaldependencies.org/he/index.html (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.name: Gender assignment on loanwords is not predictable
entries.notes: Loanwords ending in -ה or -יה are treated as feminine and take -ות; consonant-final loans are masculine and take -ים. But קומפוננטה (f.) and קומפוננט (m.) both circulate for the same English word, so agreement is genuinely unstable and cannot be derived from the English source.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Construct state (סמיכות)
en: the config file / the pump panel
entries.notes: The DEFINITENESS marker moves to the SECOND noun, and the whole phrase is definite. So קובץ הקונפיג is 'THE config file', not 'a file of the config'. Word order is head-first, the reverse of English compounds, so a word-for-word rendering inverts the modifier relation. The live log has 'ריסטייל הפאמפ פאנל' - a construct built out of two English loans - which came out as 'reset the pump panel' with the compound order accidentally right and the verb wrong.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06 ; Ozen live log (70 utterances), read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Construct state pluralises the HEAD, not the phrase
entries.notes: The head noun changes form (קבצים -> קבצי). A surface-string glossary keyed on קבצים misses קבצי entirely. This is why glossary matching must run on MORPHOLOGICALLY SEGMENTED forms.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Accusative marker את before definite objects
entries.notes: את has no English equivalent and must be deleted, not translated. It is also a homograph of את ('you', f.sg.) and of את ('spade'). Ozen's content_tokens already lists it as a stopword.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Pronominal suffixes are separate words in UD
entries.notes: UD Hebrew documents exactly this split: שלנו -> של_ + _אנחנו, and ספרו -> ספר_ + _של_ + _הוא. A suffix can therefore carry a whole pronoun that never appears as its own whitespace token.
entries.source: https://universaldependencies.org/he/index.html (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.name: Dative-experiencer frames
entries.he: נשבר לי / בא לי / נמאס לי
en: I'm fed up / I feel like / I'm sick of it
entries.notes: The grammatical subject is the situation and the human is a dative oblique. Word-for-word output ('it broke to me') is ungrammatical English. The whole clause must be re-subjectified, which is a structural transformation no lexicon entry can encode.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Hebrew has no indefinite article
entries.notes: The a/an must be INSERTED on the he->en side (and deleted on the en->he side). Ozen's REPAIR_PROMPT already documents the mirror image of this for accented English output ('I need car').
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: No present-tense copula
entries.notes: The 'is' must be inserted. Combined with the covert definite this means a two-word Hebrew clause expands to four English words, none of which are lexically present in the source.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Flexible constituent order in speech
en: there was a crash just now
entries.notes: Verb-initial order is normal in spoken Hebrew. Live log entry 0 is exactly this and was rendered well, with an inserted existential 'there was' that has no source token.
entries.source: Ozen live log (70 utterances), read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Loanwords are verbalised into native binyanim
en: to fix / to debug / to merge / to google
entries.notes: Borrowed roots are inflected in the pi'el pattern with full native conjugation (פיקססתי, מדבג, ימרג'ג). The inflected forms share no surface substring with the English source, so no amount of transliteration matching finds them. This is the single strongest argument for morphological segmentation over string matching.
entries.source: author knowledge, NOT source-verified 2026-08-06

entries.name: Unpointed orthography drops most vowels
entries.he: ספר = book / barber / he counted / story
entries.notes: Modern Hebrew is written without niqqud, so a consonant skeleton maps to several words. This is why 'tool' and 'toll', 'load' and 'lord', 'login' and 'logging' all collapse when transliterated: the distinguishing vowel is simply not written. DICTA's Nakdan exists precisely to restore diacritics.
entries.source: https://nakdanpro.dicta.org.il/ (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.name: Five letters change shape word-finally
entries.notes: A naive string comparison treats מ and ם as different characters. Ozen's phonetics.rs hebrew_key already normalises all five, which is correct and worth keeping.
entries.source: ozen src-tauri/src/phonetics.rs, read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Historically distinct letters are now homophones
entries.notes: Modern Israeli pronunciation merged several pairs, so ASR spells transliterations inconsistently. phonetics.rs already collapses ט/ת, ק/כ, ע/א and sin/samekh, and has a test pinning טסט/תסט.
entries.source: ozen src-tauri/src/phonetics.rs, read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Matres lectionis are optional
entries.notes: Written vowels are inconsistently included, especially in transliterations. phonetics.rs drops non-initial ו/י/ה/א for exactly this reason, with a test on ריפו/רפו.
entries.source: ozen src-tauri/src/phonetics.rs, read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Geresh marks non-Hebrew phonemes
entries.notes: The geresh is what makes מרג' 'merge' rather than 'marg'. ASR often omits it, so מרג and מרג' must normalise together. It is an apostrophe, which also means naive punctuation-stripping tokenisers destroy the phoneme. Ozen's content_tokens deliberately keeps the apostrophe - correct.
entries.source: ozen src-tauri/src/store.rs content_tokens, read 2026-08-06

entries.name: Clitic segmentation is a solved-ish problem with real tools
entries.notes: HebPipe reports Token F1 99.95 but Word F1 99.11 on UD Hebrew-HTB - the gap between the two IS the clitic-splitting problem. YAP does joint morphological analysis and dependency parsing but its MILA lexicon needs separate licensing for production, which is a real constraint on shipping it.
entries.source: https://github.com/amir-zeldes/HebPipe (verified 2026-08-06) ; https://github.com/OnlpLab/yap (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.name: Multiword tokens are not an edge case
entries.notes: UD Hebrew-HTB: 6143 sentences, 114648 tokens, 160195 syntactic words, and 36783 multiword tokens averaging 2.24 syntactic words each. Roughly one in three whitespace tokens in ordinary Hebrew carries more than one word. Any design that treats a whitespace token as a word is wrong a third of the time.
entries.source: https://universaldependencies.org/treebanks/he_htb/index.html (verified 2026-08-06)

entries.name: Glossary entries can fail silently
entries.notes: Google's Cloud Translation glossary documentation states that individual terms over 1024 UTF-8 bytes are silently ignored and that some terms are treated as stopwords and skipped. A glossary that is not applied looks exactly like one that is. Any glossary layer Ozen builds needs a discriminating test: feed it the term, confirm the forced rendering appears; feed it the neighbouring term, confirm it does not.
entries.source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/translate/docs/advanced/glossary (verified 2026-08-06)
